probe.area: us-universe: a point-in-time (PIT) US universe for 2014-2026, built on S&P 500 membership without API keys. It covers membership, prices for removed members, historical ticker→CIK mapping, and the cost of a full build. Everything was run live on 2026-09-25 with .venv/bin/python (pandas 2.3.3, yfinance 1.7.0, requests, bs4 4.15.0, lxml 6.1.3). Nothing was installed and nothing in the repo was changed. Code and the on-disk cache are in scratch/pit/us-universe/. The consolidated module is us_pit_universe.py. The end-to-end check is run_build.py: 30-33 s warm, log in cache/run_build.log. cold_test.py exercises every network path against an empty cache. The probe scripts are a01-a04 (membership and cross-validation), b00-b07 (prices for removed members), c01-c05 (CIK mapping), d01-d02 (SEC FTD prices) and e01-e02 (full build and bias measurement).

working.name: us_pit_universe.py (complete module, exactly as run)
working.purpose: Drop-in keyless PIT S&P 500 layer in five steps. (1) Membership comes from fja05680, patched with Wikipedia changes that fja has not picked up yet. (2) Removal events carry names and reasons, with automatic rename detection. (3) Each removed member is mapped to its historical CIK: the Wayback history of SEC company_tickers.json, validated against submissions, then Wikidata, then a name match. (4) The Yahoo series is resolved per membership spell, rejecting reused tickers. (5) SEC fails-to-deliver prices fill the gaps. run_build.py and cold_test.py both import this exact file.
working.output_shape: fja_snapshots: DataFrame indexed by date (2,720 rows, 1996-01-02..2026-08-18) with a single 'tickers' column (frozenset of str; '.' for share classes). spells_from_snapshots / patched_spells: DataFrame[ticker, start, end], where end = first day out and NaT = still in (1,265 rows patched). members_at: slice of the spells. wiki_current: 503x9 [symbol, security, sector, sub_industry, hq, date_added, cik:int, founded, sym]. wiki_changes: 409x8 [date, add_t, add_n, add_link, rem_t, rem_n, rem_link, reason], 1976-07-01..2026-09-21. removal_events: 294 rows [date, start, fja_ticker, ticker, name, link, reason, rename_to, cat]. sec_ticker_history: 34,321 (ticker, cik) pairs over 32,747 tickers [ticker, cik, title, first_seen, last_seen]. cik_lookup_index: dict of 1,010,925 normalised names to a set of CIKs. cik_for_event: (cik or None, method). yahoo_chart: dict(ok, status, err, meta, df[open, high, low, close, volume, adjclose]). resolve_yahoo: (symbol or None, label). ftd_file: DataFrame[settle, cusip, symbol, qty, desc, price] (about 34k rows per half-month). ftd_panel: the same plus px_date.
working.coverage: Removed members get a CIK for 292/294 removal events (99.3%). Yahoo covers 650/797 spells in 2014-2026 (148/294 removed spells). Member-month return coverage is 89.5% with Yahoo alone and 97.9% after adding SEC fails-to-deliver prices. See the entries below for detail.
working.notes: Every network function was run cold against an empty cache (cold_test.py): fja 0.9 s, Wikipedia 1.2 s for both pages, submissions 0.3 s, yahoo_chart 0.4-0.7 s, one FTD file 2.6 s. Passes ruff F/E9 checks. The module uses no API keys. The 5 xlsx-style caches and the 2.7 GB of total scratch cache (mostly FTD pickles) sit under cache/. Set U.CACHE to relocate them.

working.name: Wikipedia current table + 'Historical components of the S&P 500' changes table (wiki_current, wiki_changes), and cross-validation against fja
working.purpose: Supplies the current constituents with their CIK column, plus the add/remove history with names, reasons and article links. The history is used to patch fja, to name and classify removal events, and to cross-validate membership.

# a04_xval_cik.py (abridged): membership as CIK sets on 10 random business days (random.seed(7))
# fja side : spell -> CIK (current spells: Wikipedia CIK; ended spells: removal-event CIK)
# wiki side: start from today's CIK set, undo every change after d (discard CIK(add), add CIK(removed))
import random, pandas as pd
random.seed(7)
sample = sorted(random.sample(list(pd.bdate_range('2014-01-02', '2026-08-31')), 10))
# naive ticker-level backward roll (wiki_members_at in sp500_membership.py) for comparison:
def wiki_members_at(current: set, changes: pd.DataFrame, when) -> set:
    mem = set(current)
    for _, r in changes[changes['date'] > pd.Timestamp(when)].iterrows():   # newest first
        if isinstance(r['add_t'], str): mem.discard(r['add_t'])
        if isinstance(r['rem_t'], str): mem.add(r['rem_t'])
    return mem

working.purpose: Maps each removed member to the SEC CIK in force on its removal date, handling both ticker reuse and renames.

working.output_shape: ev gains two columns: 'cik' (int or NaN) and 'cik_method'.
working.coverage: Per event (294): 292 mapped (99.3%). By method: validated Wayback 275, name match 8, Wikidata 6, and 3 fallbacks to the unvalidated SEC pair (TSS, where 'TSYS' is not a name match; SBNY and FRC, bank filers that report to the FDIC and have no 10-K in EDGAR; MBC, a spin-off with no 10-K yet). The 2 unmapped are FCPT (spun off and removed within days) and CCEP (fja duplicate). An earlier probe over 304 events, adding Wikipedia-only rows, got the same 302/304. Standalone methods on those 304: the raw SEC-file pair found 289 and 284 of those validated (93.4%). Name match found 266 (87.5%). Wikidata found 195 (64.1%) and 180 validated. The SEC-file pair agrees with Wikidata on 175/190 and with name match on 248/255. The Wayback pair history covers removals from 2017-08 onward completely. For 2014-2016 removals, SEC's early snapshots still held stale pairs (e.g. LSI, COV), and name match or Wikidata covers the rest.
working.notes: Validation (validate_cik) is mandatory. The Wayback snapshots from 2017-08..2019-09 contain long-dead pairs such as ANET→Authorize.Net (CIK 1017172), KEYS→Keystone Automotive (1012393), GGP→895648 (pre-bankruptcy GGP), EVHC→1578318 and DOW→Dow Chemical while Dow Inc. was trading. In 2019-10 SEC rebuilt the file. Across all snapshots, 1,488 tickers map to more than one CIK (reuse or reorganisation): AA→4281 then 1675149, IR→1466258 then 1699150, Q→1478242 then 2058873, MON→1110783 then 1828325. Wikidata CIKs point to the article's entity, not necessarily the issuer at the time. It had 15 mismatches: AA→new Alcoa Corp, DD→DuPont de Nemours, BHI→Baker Hughes Holdings LLC, GME→1360557 (wrong), ESRX→885721 (subsidiary). The name-match route alone picks subsidiaries (PCG→75488 Pacific Gas & Electric Co.) or unrelated entities (FOX→1069996, SEDG→1867752), which is why it ranks third. Cold cost: about 571 submissions requests (531 main + 40 older pages, 64 MB) in 231 s at ≤7 req/s. cik-lookup-data.txt is an 11.5 MB compressed download (39 MB on disk, 1,060,406 lines) in 4.9 s.

working.name: run_build.py: full build end to end, plus a bias measurement against RSP
working.purpose: Runs the whole PIT build and measures the remaining survivorship bias: an equal-weight PIT portfolio against the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP), and against QuantCIO's current approach of back-filling today's members.
working.verified_code:
"""End-to-end verification of us_pit_universe.py (uses the on-disk cache; cold-run costs are in the report)."""
import time

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import us_pit_universe as U

T = time.time()
W0, W1 = pd.Timestamp("2014-01-01"), pd.Timestamp("2026-09-24")
snaps = U.fja_snapshots(max_age_h=None)
ch = U.wiki_changes(max_age_h=None)
cur = U.wiki_current(max_age_h=None)
sp = U.patched_spells(snaps, ch)
now = set(sp[sp.end.isna()].ticker.str.replace(".", "-", regex=False))
print("fja last row", snaps.index[-1].date(), "| patched current == Wikipedia table:", now == set(cur.sym), len(now))
me = pd.date_range("2014-01-31", "2026-08-31", freq="BME")
cnt = pd.Series([len(U.members_at(sp, d)) for d in me], index=me)
print("month-end member counts 2014-2026: min %d max %d mean %.1f" % (cnt.min(), cnt.max(), cnt.mean()))

ev = U.removal_events(sp, ch)
print("\nremoval events (ended spells since 2014):", len(ev), "| with Wikipedia name:", ev.name.notna().sum(),
      "| fja-only renames:", ev.rename_to.notna().sum())
print(ev["cat"].value_counts().to_string())

t0 = time.time()
pairs = U.sec_ticker_history()
lookup = U.cik_lookup_index()
wd = U.wikidata_ciks(ev.link.dropna().tolist())
res = [U.cik_for_event(r, pairs, lookup, wd) for _, r in ev.iterrows()]
ev["cik"] = [c for c, _ in res]
ev["cik_method"] = [m for _, m in res]
print(f"\nCIK mapping ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s): mapped {ev.cik.notna().sum()}/{len(ev)} ({ev.cik.notna().mean():.1%})")
print(ev.cik_method.value_counts().to_string())
print(ev[ev.cik.isna()][["date", "fja_ticker", "ticker", "name"]].to_string())

# spells -> CIK and Yahoo symbol
cur_cik = dict(zip(cur.sym, cur.cik))
cur_by_cik = U.sec_current_tickers_by_cik()
win = sp[(sp.end.isna() | (sp.end > W0)) & (sp.start <= W1)].copy()
evk = ev.set_index(["fja_ticker", "date"])
rename_map = {r.fja_ticker.replace(".", "-"): r.rename_to for _, r in ev.dropna(subset=["rename_to"]).iterrows()}
t0 = time.time()
out = []
for _, s in win.iterrows():
    e = evk.loc[(s.ticker, s.end)] if pd.notna(s.end) and (s.ticker, s.end) in evk.index else None
    cik = cur_cik.get(s.ticker.replace(".", "-")) if pd.isna(s.end) else (e.cik if e is not None else None)
    sym, how = U.resolve_yahoo(s, e, cik if pd.notna(cik) else None, cur_by_cik, rename_map)
    out.append((cik, sym, how, e["cat"] if e is not None else "current"))
win[["cik", "ysym", "yhow", "cat"]] = pd.DataFrame(out, index=win.index)
print(f"\nspells in window {len(win)} (tickers {win.ticker.nunique()}), CIK known {win.cik.notna().sum()}; Yahoo resolution {time.time() - t0:.0f}s")
print(pd.crosstab(win["cat"], win.yhow, margins=True).to_string())

# monthly returns: Yahoo adjclose; gaps -> FTD month-end prices
syms = sorted(win.ysym.dropna().unique())
adj = pd.DataFrame({s: U.yahoo_chart(s)["df"]["adjclose"] for s in syms})
adj = adj[adj.index <= W1]
mret = adj.resample("BME").last().pct_change(fill_method=None)
months = mret.index[(mret.index >= pd.Timestamp("2014-02-28")) & (mret.index <= pd.Timestamp("2026-08-31"))]
gap = win[win.ysym.isna()]
alias = dict(zip(ev.fja_ticker, ev.ticker))
gap_sym = {i: alias.get(r.ticker, r.ticker.replace(".", "-")).replace("-", "") for i, r in gap.iterrows()}
t0 = time.time()
ftd = U.ftd_panel(set(gap_sym.values()))
print(f"\nFTD panel: {len(ftd)} rows for {len(set(gap_sym.values()))} symbols ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")


def ftd_month_ret(i, s, m, prev):
    f = ftd[(ftd.symbol == gap_sym[i]) & (ftd.px_date >= s.start - pd.Timedelta(40, unit="D"))]
    p0 = f[(f.px_date > prev - pd.Timedelta(7, unit="D")) & (f.px_date <= prev)].price
    if pd.notna(s.end) and s.end <= m:
        t = f[(f.px_date <= s.end) & (f.px_date > prev)].price
    else:
        t = f[(f.px_date > m - pd.Timedelta(7, unit="D")) & (f.px_date <= m)].price
    if len(p0) and len(t):
        r = t.iloc[-1] / p0.iloc[-1] - 1
        return r if -0.6 < r < 1.0 else None
    return None


rows = []
for k, m in enumerate(months):
    prev = mret.index[mret.index.get_loc(m) - 1]
    mem = win[(win.start <= prev) & (win.end.isna() | (win.end > prev))]
    y = mret.loc[m, [s for s in mem.ysym.dropna().unique()]].dropna()
    f = [ftd_month_ret(i, s, m, prev) for i, s in mem[mem.ysym.isna()].iterrows()]
    f = [x for x in f if x is not None]

      ((bt.n_y + bt.n_f) / bt.n).mean(), ((bt.n_y + bt.n_f) / bt.n).min()))
print("annualised 2014-02..2026-08: PIT-yahoo %.4f  PIT-yahoo+FTD %.4f  RSP %.4f  today's-members %.4f"

probe.recommended_design:
1) Membership. Use S&P 500 point-in-time membership from fja05680 '(Updated).csv' snapshots (effective dates; a spell ends on the first day out), patched with rows from Wikipedia's 'Historical components' table dated after fja's last row. On every build, assert that the patched current set equals the Wikipedia current table (503 == 503 today) and that month-end counts stay within 495-510 (observed 497-506). Rebalance on the membership as of the prior close; no announcement-date information is used, so there is no look-ahead.

2) Entity key. Key every spell by SEC CIK, not ticker. Current spells take the CIK from the Wikipedia table. Ended spells take it from cik_for_event: the Wayback SEC ticker file validated against submissions, then Wikidata, then name match, with the raw SEC pair as a last resort (292/294). Collapse share classes (GOOG/GOOGL, FOX/FOXA, NWS/NWSA, DISCA/DISCK, UA/UAA) to one CIK and price a single class, so equal weights are per company.

3) Prices. For each spell, resolve_yahoo on the raw v8 chart (or yfinance with auto_adjust=False) tries the spell ticker, the ticker traded at removal, the rename chain, and the CIK's current SEC tickers with a name check. It accepts a series only if firstTradeDate is before the spell end and there is a bar within 12 days of the end. Store both 'close' (split-adjusted) and 'adjclose' (total return). This resolves 650/797 spells.

4) Gaps. For spells with no Yahoo series (146; 96 of them acquired), take monthly marks from SEC fails-to-deliver prices tracked by CUSIP: the last FTD price in the final 7 days of each month, and for the removal month the last FTD price on or before the removal date as the delisting price. That fills 86.4% of the missing member-months. Keep every member in the denominator and give each (member, month) a data_source in {yahoo, ftd, missing}. Never silently drop a member.

5) Residual biases and how to measure them on every build.
(a) Missing returns. Coverage is 89.5% of member-months with Yahoo alone and 97.9% with FTD; the gap is worst in 2014-2018 (Yahoo only 76-87%). Monitor coverage by year. Also run an equal-weight PIT portfolio against RSP adjclose monthly: today's gap is +0.15 points a year with FTD and +0.66 with Yahoo alone, TE 0.66%/0.75%. Alert if the gap exceeds 0.5 points a year or TE exceeds 1%. For reference, back-filling today's members, as QuantCIO does now, is +5.57 points a year with TE 1.87%.
(b) FTD marks are price-only and sparse. They understate total return by roughly the dividend yield of the filled names, and month-end marks can be up to 7 days stale. Measure this by re-running the RSP comparison with and without FTD fills.
(c) Terminal returns of failed firms whose trading halted (SVB's last FTD price is 106.04) are missing. Review the 4 failures by hand and use the OTC price where it exists (FRCB at 0.33), otherwise -100%.
(d) fja data quality: back-filled tickers before 2019, the CCEP/CCE duplicate (2016-01-04..05-31), the missing MBC and FCPT spells. Measure with CIK-level Jaccard against the Wikipedia backward roll on random dates (0.968-0.992 today) and require every difference to be explained by an event that created a new CIK.
(e) Yahoo lineage series (DD, CCEP, PSKY, WBD, KDP) carry predecessor history, and merger cash shows up as a distribution. Flag any daily adjclose move above 30% on a corporate-event date.
(f) The universe is still S&P 500 committee membership, not a rules-based top-N by market cap. A true PIT top-N needs point-in-time shares outstanding (XBRL dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, using first_filed) times price, which is a separate area. Index-inclusion drift around announcements is not modelled.

Requests and time:
- Membership: 4 requests, under 5 s, 7 MB (fja CSV 5.5 MB plus 2 Wikipedia pages 1.7 MB).
- Wayback SEC company_tickers.json: 1 CDX plus 94 snapshots in 443 s at 1 req/s, 77 MB raw.
- company_tickers.json plus cik-lookup-data.txt: 2 requests, about 5 s, 40 MB on disk.
- SEC submissions: 531 main plus 40 older pages = 571 requests in 231 s at ≤7 req/s, 64 MB.
- Wikipedia/Wikidata: about 12 requests, 148 s including one 429 back-off.
- Yahoo raw chart: about 611 accepted plus about 340 rejected candidates, roughly 950 requests. Measured 0.67 s per new symbol (460 in 309 s), so about 11 minutes. Disk: 111 MB for 810 chart pickles, or 145 MB as yfinance frames (237 KB per symbol, 2013-2026). A yfinance-based probe of removed tickers is 3-5 times slower (350 attempts × 3 sources took 1,640 s).
- SEC fails-to-deliver: 304 half-month zips from 2013-12 to 2026-08, about 0.8 MB each, so about 245 MB of downloads in roughly 2-4 minutes at 4 req/s. Unfiltered parsed pickles are about 3.8 MB each (about 1.15 GB); filtered to the 146 needed symbols the panel is 141k rows.

Totals: about 1,940 requests and about 25-30 minutes cold. Disk is about 0.6 GB if FTD is filtered at load time, or about 1.7 GB if every FTD pickle is kept. A warm rebuild from cache (run_build.py) takes 31-33 s. Nasdaq API is optional (about 2.5 s per symbol) and adds no coverage.
gotchas: The fja05680 file is now named 'S&P 500 Historical Components & Changes (Updated).csv', with no date suffix. Find it through the GitHub contents API, not a hard-coded name. The last data row is 2026-08-18 while the last commit is 2026-09-07, so fja lags real index changes by weeks (it missed 2026-09-21). Always patch from Wikipedia.

fja rows before 2019 come from Clenow's file and use the ticker as of about 2019, not the one traded then: ANTM in 2014 (it was WLP), AABA (YHOO), BHGE (BHI), DXC (CSC), KDP (DPS), WYND (WYN), BTUUQ (BTU), ARNC (AA). The README's claim that 'ticker names are correct on any day' does not hold before 2019. Map spells to CIK or alias them to the Wikipedia ticker.

fja data errors: CCEP and CCE are both members from 2016-01-04 to 2016-05-31 (a duplicate); the MBC spin-off (2022-12-15..19) is missing; FCPT appears for a few days in 2015-11. fja also counts share classes separately, so collapse by CIK for equal weighting.

Wikipedia's 'Selected changes' table left 'List of S&P 500 companies' on 2026-08-11 and now lives in 'Historical components of the S&P 500' (first wikitable, Parsoid absolute links). It omits symbol renames ('symbol changes are not a component change'), so a naive ticker backward roll inflates counts to 503-508 and gives only 0.88-0.97 Jaccard against fja. CIK-level Jaccard is 0.968-0.992.

Renames recorded by fja (30 since 2014) are a removal plus a same-day add with no matching Wikipedia row. removal_events detects them automatically; follow chains such as CBS→VIAC→PARA→PSKY and HCP→PEAK→DOC.

Snapshots of the SEC company_tickers.json from 2017-08 to 2019-09 on Wayback hold stale pairs from long-dead issuers (ANET→Authorize.Net, KEYS→Keystone Automotive, GGP→pre-bankruptcy GGP), and stale pairs linger about 6 months after delisting (DOW→Dow Chemical until 2019-09 while Dow Inc. traded from 2019-03). Validate every pair against submissions: a 10-K/10-Q in the 540 days before the date plus a name or formerNames match.

1,488 tickers map to more than one CIK over 2017-2026. On Yahoo, 25 of 304 removal-time tickers now belong to another issuer, including ETFs (CAM, EMC, PCL, SPLS, CSRA, INFO, FB) and new companies (LIFE→Ethos, SE→Sea Ltd, Q→Qnity, DOW→Dow Inc., SNDK→Sandisk 2025, BBBY, LB→LandBridge, ADT→ADT Inc.). A name check alone misses post-bankruptcy re-listings (BTU, NE) because the name is unchanged; the reliable test is firstTradeDate after the spell end.

The CIK→current-ticker route must include a name check. Without it TSYS (CIK 721683, no current ticker) fell through to a name lookup on 'tss', which returned TSS, Inc. (TSSI). Wikidata P5531 names the article's entity: AA→new Alcoa Corp, DD→DuPont de Nemours, BHI→Baker Hughes Holdings, and a wrong CIK for GME. Keep it third in priority.

Banks that failed in 2023 (SBNY, FRC) filed periodic reports with the FDIC, not EDGAR, so activity validation fails even for the correct CIK. Spin-offs removed before their first 10-K (MBC) also fail. Accept the SEC pair in force on the removal date as an unvalidated fallback.

Yahoo 'close' is split-adjusted and 'adjclose' also adjusts for dividends and merger cash. Lineage series carry predecessor history: DD has no jump at the 2017-09-01 DowDuPont merger, CCEP carries CCE history (2016-05-31 close drops from 51.55 to 38.81 while adjclose rises 4.75%), and PSKY carries CBS/Viacom history from 2005. The Nasdaq API is split-adjusted but not dividend-adjusted, covers active symbols only, and at most 2,513 rows (from 2016-09-23).

yfinance and the raw v8 chart come from the same backend and agreed on availability for 304/304 removal tickers. A failed yfinance call costs 2.3-5 s (YFTzMissingError), so probe candidates with the raw chart using the short UA 'Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36'.

SEC fails-to-deliver PRICE is the unadjusted close of the trading day before the settlement date. It matched Yahoo's unadjusted close on 350/350 rows (max relative error 5.6e-8), but rows exist only on days with fails, a median of 47% of business days before removal. Rows can continue after delisting (LIFE), so cap at the removal date. DESCRIPTION can contain '|'. Files before 2017-07 sit under a different path (frequently-requested-foia-document-fails-deliver-data); parse the index page.

Track fails-to-deliver prices by CUSIP: after failure the symbol gains an OTC suffix (FRC→FRCB at $0.33 on the same CUSIP 33616C100). SVB has no OTC rows after 106.04 (the 2023-03-09 close), so its terminal loss must be set by hand.
Ticker spelling differs by source: fja and Wikipedia use '.' (BRK.B, BF.B), while SEC and Yahoo use '-' (BRK-B). Fails-to-deliver symbols drop the separator (BRKB). Nasdaq uses '.'.

Wikimedia returns HTTP 429 to unauthenticated API bursts even at a handful of requests. Honour retry-after and back off; batching 50 titles per call keeps the whole Wikidata pass to about 12 requests.

Back-filling today's members (QuantCIO's current US universe) inflates equal-weight returns by about +5.6 points a year against RSP over 2014-02..2026-08 (17.02% vs 11.45%). The PIT build brings this to +0.66 points with Yahoo alone and +0.15 with fails-to-deliver fills. That tracking check should be part of every evaluation.

Hugging Face 'Stocks-Daily-Price' (paperswithbacktest) looks downloadable (HF API gated=False, shard 0 returns HTTP 200), but its card ties downloads to a paid subscription. Treat it as unusable unless the user subscribes.

The consolidated module's CACHE (scratch cache/) grew to about 2.7 GB during probing, mostly unfiltered fails-to-deliver pickles (819 MB for 213 files) and px pickles. In production, filter fails-to-deliver files to the needed CUSIPs before caching.
